s1.syndrome_frame: Bilateral ocular inflammation with recent systemic symptoms and periorbital hyperpigmentation
salient_findings: Bilateral blurred vision and ocular irritation
Bilateral punctate superficial keratitis and stromal immune ring formation
key_facts: Bilateral blurred vision and ocular irritation
Negative ocular history for trauma and previous inflammation
Slitlamp biomicroscopy revealed bilateral punctate superficial keratitis
Stromal immune ring formation with underlying keratic precipitates
Aqueous tap PCR results positive for Chikungunya virus

shortlist.label: Chikungunya virus infection
shortlist.why_kept: Positive IgM CHIKV serologic test and aqueous tap PCR results positive for Chikungunya virus

shortlist.label: Fuchs heterochromic iridocyclitis
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral ocular inflammation and keratic precipitates

shortlist.label: Herpes simplex keratitis
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral punctate superficial keratitis and stromal immune ring formation

shortlist.label: Varicella-zoster virus keratitis
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral ocular inflammation and recent systemic symptoms

shortlist.label: Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada disease
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral ocular inflammation, periorbital hyperpigmentation, and recent systemic symptoms

raw.rationale: The patient's recent fever and severe arthralgia, along with the positive IgM CHIKV serologic test and aqueous tap PCR results positive for Chikungunya virus, strongly suggest a Chikungunya virus infection. The ocular findings, including bilateral punctate superficial keratitis and stromal immune ring formation, are consistent with Chikungunya virus-associated keratitis.

rejected.label: Fuchs heterochromic iridocyclitis
rejected.why: No heterochromia or chronic inflammation was mentioned

rejected.label: Herpes simplex keratitis
rejected.why: Aqueous tap PCR results were negative for human herpesviruses 1 and 2

rejected.label: Varicella-zoster virus keratitis
rejected.why: Aqueous tap PCR results were negative for varicella-zoster virus

rejected.label: Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada disease
rejected.why: No mention of granulomatous uveitis, skin, or hair findings typical of VKH
